name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the Scotland of the East for its rolling hills, colonial charm, and vibrant Khasi culture.
facts: Named after the deity Lei Shyllong on Shillong Peak
Former summer capital of Assam during British rule
Home to Police Bazar, Ward's Lake, and Don Bosco Museum

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest point in Meghalaya at about 1966 m, offering panoramic views of Shillong city and surrounding hills; sacred site for Khasi rituals.
facts: About 10 km from Shillong city center
Highest peak in the state
Site of annual rituals to U Shyllong by Mylliem priests

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong, named after a rock formation once resembling an elephant; set amid fern-covered rocks and greenery.
facts: Local name Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew meaning three-step falls
Approximately 12 km from Shillong
Popular short stop on the way to Cherrapunji

name: Ward's Lake
description: Artificial horseshoe-shaped lake in central Shillong with a bridge, gardens, and boating; a popular local picnic and evening hangout spot.
facts: Also known as Pollock's Lake or Nan Polok
Located near Raj Bhavan
Ideal for leisurely walks and photography

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
description: One of India's largest museums showcasing the cultures, lifestyles, and artifacts of Northeast India's indigenous communities.
facts: Located in Mawlai, Shillong
Houses extensive collections on Khasi, Garo, Jaintia and other tribes
Important cultural education center

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Famous for being one of the wettest places on Earth, featuring dramatic cliffs, waterfalls, caves, and living root bridges on the southern plateau edge.
facts: Local name Sohra; formerly Cherrapunjee
Perched at about 1430 m overlooking Bangladesh plains
Gateway to Nohkalikai Falls and root bridges

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at about 340 m, plunging from the Cherrapunji plateau into a turquoise pool amid steep cliffs and forests.
facts: Named after a local legend of a woman named Likai
Fed by monsoon rains on the plateau
Best viewed from designated viewpoints near Sohra

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Segmented waterfall cascading in multiple parallel streams down limestone cliffs near Mawsmai, offering panoramic views toward the Bangladesh plains.
facts: Also called Seven Sisters Falls
Most spectacular during and after monsoon
Located near Mawsmai village

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone show cave near Sohra with lighted passages, stalactites, and stalagmites; suitable for casual visitors including families.
facts: About 150 m of lighted passages
One of the easiest caves in Meghalaya to explore
Approximately 6 km from Sohra town

name: Arwah Cave
description: Limestone cave near Sohra known for fossilized marine shells and fish bones visible in the walls; features a short forest approach and lit interiors.
facts: Contains prehistoric marine fossils
Optional guide recommended
Part of the Sohra cave circuit

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge
description: Unique two-tiered living root bridge in Nongriat village, grown from Ficus elastica roots by Khasi communities over generations; reached by a steep trek of thousands of steps.
facts: Only double-decker living root bridge of its kind
Estimated over 180 years old
Trek from Tyrna village involves ~3500 steps each way

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Widely known as Asia's cleanest village, featuring living root bridges, a balancing rock, and community-managed eco-tourism near the Bangladesh border.
facts: Declared cleanest village in Asia by Discover India magazine
Features a single living root bridge and skywalk viewpoint
About 90 km from Shillong

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic cliffside viewpoint meaning 'end of hills' in Khasi, offering sweeping views of deep valleys, winding rivers, and layered hills about 25 km from Shillong.
facts: Meaning 'end of hills' in Khasi
Popular for sunrise and panoramic views
Optional trek down into the valley possible

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient Khasi sacred grove protected by traditional beliefs, rich in biodiversity, medicinal plants, and monoliths; entry requires a local guide.
facts: Protected by belief in resident deity Labasa
No removal of anything from the forest allowed
About 25 km from Shillong; starting point of David Scott Trail

name: Mawsynram
description: Town known as one of the wettest places on Earth, featuring lush landscapes, caves like Mawjymbuin with Shiva-linga shaped stalagmites, and traditional archery culture.
facts: Records some of the highest average annual rainfall in the world
About 15 km west of Cherrapunji
Home to Mawjymbuin Cave with notable speleothems

name: Kongthong Whistling Village
description: Unique Khasi village where residents communicate using personal whistled tunes instead of names, set amid scenic hills with trekking trails and living root bridges.
facts: Each person has a unique whistled tune used as a name
Promotes eco-tourism and cultural experiences
Located in the southern part of East Khasi Hills
